candidateAdjudications.reason: This is the object-and-manner tail of "It can assign settings dynamically using normal Python syntax": a direct object ('settings'), an adverb ('dynamically'), and a gerund phrase with its own object ('using normal Python syntax'). It is ordinary clause structure, not a stacked noun run, and the only real noun group in it, 'normal Python syntax', is a transparent adjective-adjective-noun phrase with one obvious reading. The heuristic's word count triggered on a verb phrase, not a noun pile.

Third bullet of the same parallel list; the intervening code block makes the heuristic see "For example::" as the previous sentence, but a reader tracks the list structure and resolves "It" to the settings file. Referent is unambiguous.

"When you use Django, you have to tell it which settings you're using" — only Django can be told something, and it is the immediately preceding subject of the clause. The settings are the content of the telling, not the addressee.
